title: Projected amorphous topological insulators
abstract: We introduce projected amorphous topological insulators (PATIs) that despite containing only a fraction ($x$) of otherwise randomly selected {\it disconnected} sites of a parent crystal, feature a quantized global topological invariant ({\it strong} PATIs) when its effective Hamiltonian is constructed by integrating out the residual sites of the original lattice. Within the topological regime of the parent model, additionally, there exists a critical $x$ below which such systems foster a {\it fragile} PATI that only supports quantized local topological marker on a small fraction of sites therein. Both strong and fragile PATIs accommodate in-gap modes near the boundary. The system also hosts a normal insulator in the entire trivial parameter regime of the lattice-based model for any $x$, devoid of gapless boundary modes, for which both global topological invariant and local topological marker vanish. We demonstrate these {\it possibly} generic outcomes by starting with a parent square lattice-based model for time-reversal symmetry breaking insulators. Then the strong-to-fragile PATI quantum phase transition, tunable via $x$, is characterized by the {\it mean} correlation length exponent $ν\in (1.00,1.46)$.
summary: This paper introduces Projected Amorphous Topological Insulators (PATIs) to study topological phases in disordered materials. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian derived from a parent crystal, the authors distinguish between strong, fragile, and trivial topological states based on quantized global and local invariants. The work characterizes a quantum phase transition between these states, providing a theoretical framework for disorder-induced topological phenomena.
main_problem: To investigate the possibility of realizing topological insulators in the absence of crystalline order, specifically on amorphous lattices.
main_result: The study identifies three distinct phases—strong PATIs, fragile PATIs, and Projected Amorphous Normal Insulators (PANIs)—and characterizes the quantum phase transition between the strong and fragile phases using a specific correlation length exponent.
method: The analysis constructs an effective Hamiltonian by integrating out residual sites from a parent crystal lattice and uses topological invariants (global and local) to diagnose the phases.
model_or_system: The system is the Projected Amorphous Topological Insulator (PATI), formed by randomly selecting a fraction ($x$) of sites from a parent crystal lattice (e.g., a square lattice for time-reversal symmetry breaking insulators).

important_parameters: The concentration fraction $x$, which tunes the system between strong and fragile topological regimes, and the critical concentration $x_c$.
main_assumptions: The method is claimed to be general and applicable to any dimension, symmetry class, and parent crystal lattice.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the physical model and the effective Hamiltonian, analyzing the topological invariants to distinguish between strong, fragile, and trivial phases, and finally characterizing the quantum phase transition via scaling laws and critical exponents.
why_interesting: The concept of topological protection surviving in highly disordered, amorphous media is crucial for developing robust quantum hardware, linking topological physics to disorder physics.
